record.paper_title: On Open Problems in Biological Network Visualization
record.original_question: In biological network visualization, suppose a pathway or other biological network is represented as a graph G1=(V,E1), and correlation data over the same biological entities induces a weighted correlation graph G2=(V,E2) on the same node set V. The correlation edges should represent only statistically significant relationships, such as significant up- or down-regulation of co-expressed genes or proteins, and entities with multiple annotations may be treated as correlated when enough annotations correspond, for example by genotype, time value, or biological replicate number. How can one compute a layout that either draws the union of the two graphs or draws two aligned layouts with identical node coordinates, so that both the original network G1 and the correlation graph G2 are clearly displayed, the two edge sets E1 and E2 are visually distinguishable, and any pre-existing layout of G1 is preserved as closely as possible while the correlation structure is still emphasized?

evidence.quote: Investigators are then interested in a graphical representation that highlights the interrelation between the connectivity structure of pairs or subsets of nodes in the original network and their correlation.

We seek either a layout of the union graph G = (V,E1 ∪ E2), in which the given network G1 and the correlations are clearly displayed, or two disjoint layouts, in which the coordinates of the nodes in both layouts are identical.
In the first case, a challenging task is to provide a layout which clearly emphasizes the two different edge sets E1 and E2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let V be a finite set of biological entities (e.g., genes or proteins). Suppose we are given:

(1) A biological network graph G1 = (V, E1) representing known structural relationships such as a pathway, possibly equipped with a pre-existing layout L1 : V → R^2 that assigns each node a position in the plane.

(2) A weighted correlation graph G2 = (V, E2, w) on the same node set V, where each edge {u,v} ∈ E2 carries a weight w(u,v) ∈ R representing a statistically significant correlation between u and v (for instance, significant co-up-regulation or co-down-regulation of expression, or sufficient agreement of annotations across attributes such as genotype, time point, or biological replicate). Edges that fail a chosen significance threshold are excluded from E2.

The problem is to design an algorithm that produces either:
(a) a single planar drawing of the union graph G = (V, E1 ∪ E2), in which the two edge sets E1 and E2 are rendered so as to be visually distinguishable; or
(b) two drawings of G1 and G2 respectively that share an identical node-coordinate map φ : V → R^2,

subject to the following objectives:

(i) Both the structure of G1 and the correlation structure of G2 should be clearly readable in the resulting drawing(s).
(ii) The drawing should deviate from the given pre-existing layout L1 of G1 as little as possible, under a suitable quantitative measure (e.g., sum of squared displacements ∑_{v∈V} ‖φ(v) − L1(v)‖^2).
(iii) The correlation edges E2 (especially those with high |w|) should be emphasized, for example by minimizing a stress-like functional that penalizes large geometric distance between strongly correlated node pairs.

Formulate and solve: produce an algorithm (and an associated objective function balancing (ii) and (iii)) that, given (G1, L1, G2, w), outputs a coordinate map φ : V → R^2 (and a rendering style for the two edge sets in case (a)) meeting the above criteria, together with guarantees on readability and on preservation of L1.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as one of the open challenges in biological network visualization concerning correlation-aware layouts. No definitive algorithmic solution with formal guarantees appears in the literature; the area has seen heuristic tools (e.g., Cytoscape plugins, edge-bundling and constrained stress majorization), but a recognized solution meeting all stated criteria has not been identified. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Open Problems in Biological Network Visualization
status_evidence.snippet: Lists correlation-aware layouts as an open problem in biological network visualization.
status_evidence.claim: Problem is identified as open in the original venue.
